title: Alaska Airlines adds four new cities to its Seattle network, plus a new seasonal nonstop route to Guadalajara, Mexico
summary: Alaska will launch its first nonstop service between Anchorage and Tokyo Narita* next spring, creating a convenient new connection between Alaska and the Asia-Pacific region.
body_markdown:
Alaska Airlines is making its hometown hub even stronger with five new nonstop routes to high-demand destinations in 2027, giving Seattle travelers more options to travel without a connection. Beginning next spring and summer, guests can fly nonstop to Charlotte, North Carolina; Jacksonville, Florida; Norfolk, Virginia; Des Moines, Iowa; and Guadalajara, Mexico. For Jacksonville, Norfolk and Des Moines, the service will mark the first-ever nonstop connection to Seattle.


The additions will give Seattle travelers more destinations to reach nonstop across the country and into Mexico, bringing Alaska’s network from the Emerald City to 119 nonstop destinations. The new service marks Alaska’s biggest summer launch yet in Seattle, strengthening the hub with new destinations and more convenient options across the network. The new routes give guests more ways to experience Alaska Airlines thoughtful care, meaningful choice and generous loyalty.


For travel within the U.S. and to Mexico, guests can choose from a range of experiences based on the comfort,


flexibility


and amenities they want, from Main Cabin to extra-legroom Premium Class and First Class.


First Class guests enjoy complimentary chef-curated meals. Guests in First Class, Premium Class and Main Cabin can pre-order fresh, chef-crafted meals through the Alaska Airlines app up to


14 days


in advance. Guests can relax and enjoy a range of beverages onboard, including sodas, beer,


wine


and premium spirits


.
